threads.thread_goal: Align on current journey map, key gaps, and overall pathway design.

messages.text: Morning all. I have pulled together a first pass of the current client journey from referral to employment for the Integrated Employment Readiness Pathway for Vulnerable Clients. It is based on 10 recent cases and is linked in A1, with notes against T1. The map shows referral, initial assessment, ad hoc health checks, sporadic job search support, then placement and limited follow up. Can you review and highlight anything that feels off or missing, especially around moves and first days in placement?

Thanks for sharing. Looking at A1 and your notes under T1, the biggest gap I see is that employment prep only really starts once housing and health are mostly sorted. For many clients that means months of drift. Could we sketch a pathway where light-touch employment readiness starts much earlier, even while housing or health issues are being stabilised?

I went through the journey in A1 as well. One thing I noticed is we do not show clearly when we explain rights and consent to clients. It kind of appears at assessment but then disappears. For T2, when we design the holistic assessment template, can we build in a clear step where we revisit consent before sharing information with employers or movers?

From the moves side, the map in A1 shows a single handover from social worker to mover just before relocation. In practice, we often get very little context about the client, especially around anxiety, mobility, or family dynamics. That is a gap. For T6, could we add a standard pre-move briefing stage where we get a short case summary and any safeguarding flags?

I agree with that. Looking at A1, health checks are shown as a one-off. For some clients we need more than one contact, especially around stress before a move or starting work. Maybe the new pathway could have a short health and wellbeing check before moves and again after the first week in placement?

I noticed another pattern in the T1 cases: we do not have a clear step where we check if the job role still matches the client goals after housing or health changes. Sometimes people end up in placements that no longer fit. Could we add a review stage between initial employment plan and final placement confirmation?

Agree on starting employment readiness earlier. Based on what you all said, I am proposing these main stages for the new pathway draft in A1: 1) Referral and triage, 2) Holistic assessment and consent using T2, 3) Early light-touch employment readiness, 4) Health and wellbeing screening and stabilisation, 5) Housing or relocation planning, 6) Placement matching and review, 7) Move and first days in work, 8) Ongoing in-work support and review. Does this feel workable, or are we missing a key stage?

That structure works for me. I would just make the early employment readiness stage more explicit: things like confidence building, basic routine, and understanding what work might look like. That will link directly into T3 later. Maybe we call stage 3 'Foundations for work and confidence' so it is clear it is not just CV writing.

I like the stages. I am not sure where we put explaining the whole pathway to clients. Should that be in stage 1 or 2? I am thinking ahead to T7 and A8, where we will have the client information pack. Maybe we say we always give the pack at triage and then go over it again at assessment?

On the move and first days in work stage, can we make sure the safe relocation checklist from T5 and A5 is built in as a required step, not optional? That is where we can protect belongings and dignity, and also pick up any last-minute worries before the first shift.

For the health and wellbeing stage, I would like us to keep it short but focused, because staff time is tight. Maybe a brief screening using what we will define in T4 and A4, plus a clear route to clinical services if needed. We can then repeat a shorter check after the first week in work.

On coordination, I think T6 and A3 should sit across all stages, but especially at handovers: after assessment, before move, and after first week in work. Maybe we define those three as mandatory handover points in the protocol.

Let me summarise the main gaps we have surfaced from T1 and A1 so far: 1) Employment support starts too late and is not continuous. 2) Handovers between roles are weak, especially before moves and after first days in work. 3) Client rights, consent, and expectations are not explained consistently across the journey. Are these the right top three to prioritise in the pilot design, given our 21-day deadline?
Those three resonate with what I see day to day. If we fix them, it will also make T3, T7, and T8 much more effective. I would keep them as our main focus for the pilot.

I agree with those three. I would just add that we should be careful not to overload clients with information when we fix the rights and consent gap. Maybe we can test the wording in A8 with a small group first, but the priority itself makes sense.

From my side, the handover gap is the one that causes the most stress on move days. If we can strengthen that through T6 and A3, I am happy for it to be one of the top three. The other two you listed also feel right.
I am ok with those three priorities. The health checks we add in T4 can sit inside them, especially around handovers and client wellbeing during moves and first days in work.

Thanks all. To close this out: 1) We are agreeing the main stages of the new pathway as the eight-stage structure I outlined in M7, with the tweak that stage 3 is called Foundations for work and confidence and includes early light-touch support. 2) We are confirming the top three priority gaps for the pilot as: earlier and continuous employment readiness, stronger handovers across roles, and consistent explanation of rights, consent, and expectations. I will update A1 and start drafting T2 and T6 to reflect this.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise assessment, health screening, and safeguarding tools.

messages.text: Following on from the pathway stages we agreed, I have uploaded drafts for the holistic assessment and consent template (T2), the health screening checklist (T4), and the safeguarding and incident reporting flow (T9). They are reflected in A2, A4, and A7. Can you review with a focus on what is realistic to use in short appointments and during busy shifts?

I have gone through the health screening part in A4 and the T4 draft. It looks good but might be a bit long for one visit. Could we split it into a core set of questions we always ask, and an optional section for when there is more time or higher concern?

On A2 and T2, I like that we have sections for social, health, skills, and employment goals. I am a bit unsure about the wording in the consent section. It might be hard for clients with low literacy. Could we simplify the language and maybe add a short script so staff know how to explain it in plain terms?

Agree on the consent wording. We can align it with what we plan to say in the client information pack in A8 and T7, so clients hear the same message in writing and in conversation. I can take a pass at simplifying the text if that helps.

Looking at A7 and T9, the incident types and thresholds make sense, but I wonder if we need clearer examples for staff who are less familiar with safeguarding. For instance, what counts as a low-level concern versus something that needs immediate escalation?

From the moves side, I would find it helpful if A7 included a short section on incidents during transport or moves, like lost belongings, unsafe access, or distress during the journey. T9 mentions moves but it is brief. Could we expand that part a bit?

I also think examples would help. Maybe we can add a one-page annex to A7 with short scenarios: one for health concerns, one for emotional distress, one for something that happens at the workplace, and one during a move.

Good point on length. For T4 and A4, I can mark a core section that must always be completed, and an extended section for when there are red flags or more time. We will keep the core to a few key questions on physical health, mental wellbeing, medication, and mobility.

On T2, I noticed we ask about employment goals but not about fears or worries about work. For many clients, that is just as important. Could we add a short question like: What concerns do you have about starting or returning to work?
I like that addition. It will also help us tailor the workshops in T3. Maybe we can add a tick-box list of common worries plus space to write more, so it is easier to complete quickly.

On the safeguarding flow in T9 and A7, can we clarify who is responsible for logging incidents in the shared system and who leads on follow up? Right now it says the lead professional, but that might be interpreted differently by each role.

Agree. For incidents during moves, I can log the basic details, but I would expect the social worker to lead on follow up with the client and any other agencies. Maybe A7 can spell that out so it is clear.

For health-related incidents, I can record the clinical details and immediate actions, but I would still expect the social worker to coordinate the wider safeguarding response. So I support making that explicit in T9.

On the holistic assessment and consent template in T2 and A2, I have now: 1) simplified the consent wording, 2) added a short script for staff, 3) included a question on worries about work with tick boxes and free text, and 4) made sure we capture how clients prefer to be contacted. Are there any remaining concerns before we say this is ready for pilot use?
From my side, the updated T2 and A2 look workable. The script will really help newer staff. I am happy for us to use this version in the pilot.
The revised T4 and A4 with core and extended sections feel manageable now. I can see myself using the core part in a short visit. I am ok for us to go ahead with this for the pilot.

With the clarifications you added, A7 and T9 now state that: the person who first notices the incident logs it, and the allocated social worker leads on follow up and multi-agency coordination. That works for me and should reduce confusion.

To wrap this up: 1) We are approving the holistic assessment and consent template in T2 and A2 for pilot use, with the simplified wording and added questions. 2) We are agreeing on the safeguarding and incident reporting flow in T9 and A7, including examples and clear responsibilities for logging and follow up. I will post the final links in the channel and note that these are the versions to use in the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Shape the workshop programme and client-facing information pack.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first outline for the employment readiness workshops under T3 and a draft of the client-facing information pack under T7, which is reflected in A8. The workshop plan currently has four sessions: 1) Foundations for work and confidence, 2) Understanding your strengths and interests, 3) Practical steps to starting work, and 4) Rights, support, and staying well in work. Can you take a look and see if this structure fits with the pathway we agreed?

I like the four-session structure in T3. For clients with low literacy, some of the activities in session 2 and 3 might be too text-heavy. Could we add more visual or discussion-based options, like picture cards for strengths or simple role plays for talking to an employer?

Looking at A8 and T7, the information pack covers what the pathway is, what clients can expect, and their rights and consent. It is clear, but maybe a bit long. Could we create a one-page summary at the front with icons, then keep the detailed sections behind for those who want more?

In session 4 of T3, could we include a short part on managing health and stress at work, and when to ask for adjustments? That would link well with the health screening in T4 and the safeguarding guidance in A7.

From the moves perspective, it might help if session 3 or 4 briefly covers what happens on move day and the first commute, linking to the checklist in A5 and T5. Clients often worry about how they will actually get to work and what to expect on that first day.

On A8, could we make sure the section on safeguarding and incident reporting is short and reassuring, focusing on how clients can raise concerns and what will happen if they do? We can keep the detailed staff process in A7.

Good call on the activities. I will adjust T3 so that each session has at least one low-text option: picture-based strengths cards, group discussions, and simple scenarios instead of long worksheets. We can also build in time for interpreters where needed.

On A8 and T7, I can create a front-page summary with icons for the main stages of the pathway, what clients can expect, and key rights. The rest of the pack can give more detail for those who want it. We will also keep the language as plain as possible.

For the workshop feedback form in T3, I drafted a simple version with smiley faces and a few short questions. Could someone check that it captures what we need for T12 later, like whether clients feel more ready for work and understand their rights?

I have reviewed the feedback form in T3. It covers confidence, understanding of the pathway, and whether clients know who to contact with concerns. That will feed nicely into T12. I suggest we add one open question about what they would change in the sessions.

I am happy to help with a short section in session 4 on managing health at work. We can keep it practical: taking breaks, medication, who to talk to if things get hard, and how adjustments can be requested.
If helpful, I can provide a short description for A8 about what happens on move day and the first commute, in simple steps. That way the workshop content and the pack tell the same story.

Based on your feedback, the updated T3 now has: 1) four sessions as originally proposed, 2) low-text and visual activities in each session, 3) a health and stress segment in session 4, and 4) a short piece on move day and first commute linked to A5 and T5. Any objections to locking this structure for the pilot?
No objections from me. The four sessions cover what I see clients needing most, and the activities feel doable.
I am comfortable with this structure as well. It aligns with the pathway stages and supports the priorities we set earlier. Happy to sign this off for the pilot.

On A8, the revised draft with the front-page summary and clearer safeguarding section reads much better. It explains the pathway, rights, and consent in a way that should work for most clients. I do not see any major gaps.

If there are no further comments, I suggest we: 1) lock the four-session workshop structure in T3 as our pilot model, and 2) sign off the current version of the client information pack in T7 and A8 for printing and sharing with clients at triage and assessment.

Agreed. Let us record that: 1) the four-session workshop programme in T3 is our confirmed structure for the pilot, and 2) the client-facing information pack in T7 and A8 is approved for distribution. I will note this in our summary and share the final links.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on logistics for moves, workplace transitions, and employer engagement.

messages.text: I have drafted the safe relocation and workplace transition checklist under T5, now reflected in A5. It covers home moves, first commute, and first day in the workplace. Also, there is an initial list of potential community employers under T11. Can we review both so we can finalise logistics for the pilot?

Looking at A5 and T5, the checklist is thorough. For the first commute section, could we add an option for a practice run with the client where possible, or at least a clear travel plan with timings and backup options?

On the employer list in T11, I see five employers: two cafes, a warehouse, a charity shop, and a cleaning company. Have we checked with them about what support they can offer to clients who might need adjustments or flexible hours?

I have had initial conversations with all five employers in T11. Three have confirmed they can offer some flexibility and basic support, and two are still considering. I will document the expectations and support needs for each employer in the T11 summary.

On A5, could we add a quick health and stress check before the move starts and after arrival, especially for clients with mobility issues or anxiety? That would link with T4 and help us spot problems early.

For safeguarding, can we make sure A5 and T5 clearly reference the incident reporting flow in A7 and T9? For example, if something happens during a move or first day, the mover or employment support worker knows exactly how to log and escalate it.

On the employer side, we should also think about how we prepare them. Maybe a short briefing note or call covering the pathway, safeguarding basics, and who to contact if they have concerns. That could sit alongside T11 and link back to A1 and A7.

I can add a step in A5 and T5 for either a practice run or a detailed travel plan, depending on what is realistic. We will include checking accessibility, travel time, and what to do if transport is disrupted.

Quick update on T11: the two employers who were unsure have now confirmed interest, provided we keep placements small at first and offer a clear contact point. That gives us five employers for the pilot, with different types of roles.

That mix of employers in T11 sounds good. It gives us options for different abilities and interests. We just need to be clear with clients that these are pilot placements and that we will review how it goes.
Happy to support with the quick health checks around moves. We just need to keep them short so they fit into the schedule. Maybe two or three key questions and a simple rating of stress or pain.
I have added a line in A5 and T5 that says: if any concern arises during move or first day, follow the safeguarding and incident reporting flow in A7 and T9. That should help keep things consistent.

I can draft a short employer briefing linked to T11, summarising the pathway from A1, basic safeguarding expectations from A7, and who to contact in case of issues. We can share it before placements start.

With these changes, the T5 checklist in A5 now covers: pre-move briefing, health and stress checks, protecting belongings and dignity, practice run or travel plan, and clear links to safeguarding. Are we comfortable approving this as the standard for the pilot?
From a safeguarding and coordination point of view, the updated T5 and A5 look solid and workable. I am happy for us to use this checklist in the pilot.
On employers, we now have five confirmed for T11. I suggest we include all five in the pilot but start with small numbers of clients in each, so we can learn what works before scaling up.
Including all five employers with small numbers sounds sensible. It will give us a better picture of different settings without overcommitting any single employer.

To summarise: 1) we are approving the safe relocation and workplace transition checklist in T5 and A5 for the pilot, and 2) we are confirming the initial set of five community employers in T11 as our pilot partners, starting with small numbers in each. I will capture this in the project summary.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, evaluation, and team rituals for the pilot.

messages.text: We now need to finalise how we will track outcomes and run reviews during the pilot. Drafts are ready for the outcome and attendance tracker under T8, reflected in A6, and the pilot evaluation plan under T12. T10 has a first sketch of staff micro-training sessions. Can you review and comment on what data we should definitely track and how often we should check in as a team?

Looking at A6 and T8, we currently track attendance, session completion, and employment outcomes. I suggest we also track: 1) whether clients complete the full pathway or drop out, and 2) basic reasons for drop-out where known. That will help us improve the pathway.

On T12, the evaluation plan mentions client feedback from the workshop forms in T3 and a short end-of-pathway survey. Could we also include a quick check-in call or message a month after clients start work, to see how they are doing?

For health and wellbeing, could A6 include a simple rating at key points, like before move, after first week in work, and at the end of the pilot? Something like feeling worse, same, or better compared to before.

From the moves side, it would be useful if A6 or T8 captured whether the move and first commute went as planned, and if any incidents were logged in A7 and T9. That way we can see patterns and improve the checklist in A5.

On team rituals, T10 suggests short micro-training sessions and T12 proposes a mid-pilot and end-pilot review. I would add a brief weekly async check-in in this channel where each role posts what they are seeing, any issues, and quick wins.
I have updated A6 and T8 to include completion status and reasons for drop-out where known. We will keep reasons high-level and anonymised, like health, housing, work fit, or other.
On T12, I have added a one-month post-start check-in, which can be a call or message depending on client preference. We will record basic notes and whether any extra support was needed.
The simple wellbeing rating has been added to A6 at three points. I will help colleagues understand how to use it during the micro-training in T10.
Thanks for adding the move and commute outcome fields in A6. That will make it easier to see if certain routes or timings cause more issues.

In terms of indicators, the updated A6 and T8 now track: attendance, session completion, pathway completion or drop-out with reasons, employment outcomes, wellbeing ratings at key points, move and commute outcomes, and whether any incidents were logged. Are there any other essentials we are missing for the pilot?
That list covers what I would expect for a pilot. Anything more detailed might be hard to keep up with in practice.
I agree. As long as we actually fill in A6 consistently, this should give us a good picture of what is working and where clients struggle.

On cadence, I propose: 1) weekly async check-in in this channel, 2) a short mid-pilot review meeting using T12, and 3) an end-of-pilot review meeting, plus a short written summary. That should be enough without overloading people.
Weekly async check-ins sound manageable. If we keep them short and focused, they should help us spot issues early.
I can commit to posting a brief update each week on moves and first commutes, including any incidents or near misses.

On T10, the micro-training plan currently has three short sessions: 1) using the assessment and consent tools in T2 and A2, 2) using the health screening and move checklist in T4 and A5, and 3) using the safeguarding flow in T9 and A7 and filling in A6. Any changes needed before we schedule these into existing shifts?
Those three micro-training sessions cover the key tools. I would just keep each one to 20–30 minutes so they fit into handover times.
Agreed. We can also record a short screen walkthrough of A6 so people can revisit it later without needing another session.

To close this thread: 1) we are agreeing that the key indicators and data to track during the pilot are those now captured in A6 and T8, including attendance, completion, outcomes, wellbeing, move and commute results, and incidents; and 2) we are confirming the cadence and format of check-ins and reviews as weekly async updates, plus mid-pilot and end-pilot reviews as set out in T12. I will finalise T8, T10, and T12 accordingly.
